skin_texture.roughness_basis: Reconstructed engineering value, not measured from a period person or calibrated capture.
skin_texture.identity_basis: Cleared reusable generic skin atlas; not a likeness, attested complexion, or source identifying any named/reconstructed resident.
skin_texture.uv_status: Source atlas and UV registration viewed in source diagnostics; final Blender export/LOD render validation remains outstanding.
skin_texture.female_appearance_status: The same author's female bronze atlas (skins01, CC0), replacing the male one whose beard shadow read as a man's jaw at 3 m (T-3434); photographic qualification remains open.

hair_component.appearance_basis: Shared cleared CC0 short04 source fitted to existing Otis/Joseph/Martin bodies; hair/part/color are reconstructed choices, no period hairstyle attestation or individual likeness.

eye_components.source_basis: Actual helper centers/axes; original opaque sclera/iris/pupil, reconstructed dimensions and brown color, not resident facts

label: Reconstructed girl of the 1812 town, about six to ten, in a high-waisted short-sleeved frock to above the ankle in faded rose printed cotton with a white linen pinafore over it, dark shoes, bare head, on an 8-year child body of the shared portable rig
basis: Original garments on a cleared MakeHuman hm08 child body (T-3465): shells offset from the body's own surface, a skirt lofted round its own sections, pieces cut from a garment's own surface, after the period pictures named in the sources and the children's research (docs/RESEARCH/people-1812-3465/day.json "dress"; docs/RESEARCH/people-1812-3461/dress.json "Children 2-12 and infants"). Seams, ease, lengths and colours are reconstructed. Complete source anatomy remains unchanged beneath clothing.
source_scope: Eastern portraits and objects of about 1805-1815 (the Met): Joshua Johnson's Rutter children and Emma Van Name (Baltimore, about 1805), the Beecher child's frock (about 1813), the Pixler family (about 1815). None shows a child at Chicago; Wau-Bun and Quaife place the children in the town and record nothing of their dress. No pixels or traced shapes enter the asset.

reference_summary.name: a girl of the 1812 town, about six to ten

body_parameters.height_basis: CDC 2000 stature-for-age, girls, 10th centile at 96.5 months (120.5 cm; statage.csv), the centile the children's research (T-3465) takes for every child of 1812 after Steckel 1985 and Komlos 2003. The kit draws each girl at her own height (0.88-1.12 of this). Not a recorded height.
body_parameters.age_basis: Engineering body at 8 (MakeHuman child 7/9, baby 2/9 between its 10- and 1-year anchors); no girl of the town is named by the asset and no age is read. One 8-year body stands for girls about 5.5 to 10.5 at the 10th centile; see the notes file.
body_parameters.shape_basis: CC0 female child and baby macro targets; equal software-category blend is engineering only, not inferred ancestry or a portrait.

proof_variants.body_basis: CC0 child graphical body and a cleared generic young skin atlas are reconstructed authoring choices. The child is anonymous: a child of the town whose presence Quaife (1913, App. IX) and Wau-Bun record, not any one of them; no complexion, height, face or outfit of anyone is asserted.

child_components.evidence_choice: The research proposes a high-waisted frock to the ankle with a pinafore for girls about 4-13; the frock rests on the Rutter girl and Emma Van Name, the pinafore is reconstructed. A faded rose printed cotton is taken over white so that the girls are not all in white beside the toddlers.

provenance.source_scope: A high-waisted frock with short sleeves and a round neck, on the Rutter girl (white) and Emma Van Name (pink, spotted), about 1805. The puffed sleeve, the neck's depth and the faded rose (a flat colour standing for a small printed cotton) are reconstructed.

The frock's skirt falling from the high waist to the ankle (the Rutter girl; the Beecher frock). Hemmed a little above the ankle for a girl about the house in August; fullness and gathers are reconstructed.

A pinafore over the frock for work and play: the research (dress.json "Children 2-12", day.json girl_frock_pinafore_1812) marks it reconstructed, and no picture read shows one. A bib on the breast and a broad apron round the front and sides to below the knee, white linen.
Shoes: the Rutter and Van Name girls wear red; a dark brown leather is taken for a frontier girl's everyday pair. A working family's girl barefoot in summer is not made.
